title: EXP-087 - Hello World Part 5 Sections 7-8: Create the FX_CustomerID In Collection Validator
objective: Follow hello-world-pt5.md Sections 7-8 (10:38-13:06), adapted to FX_ names and User scope. Through the Web Designer Edit > Validator global-object dialog (docs/mongoose/guides/global-objects-additional.md "Creating a Validator object"), create one Validator: Name FX_CustomerID; Type In Collection; Parameters: IDO FX_HelloWorld01; Set Prop outputs Target %1 = Value FX_Label and Target %2 = Value FX_Address; In Collection Only Property FX_Code; Error Message mIsNotAValid. The tutorial's Customer IDO maps to FX_HelloWorld01, ID to FX_Code, Name to FX_Label and Address to FX_Address (EXP-078). The spoken error message "m is not a valid" is taken as the standard message ID mIsNotAValid (unverified); no string is created for it. Commit every field with Tab before OK. Read the validator back, perform one Designer Save, close and reopen the FX_Orders Designer Form once and read it back again. The component class (Section 9) and its use on FX_Orders are later experiments. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt5.md Sections 7-8 and their transcript lines (10:38-13:06), docs/mongoose/guides/global-objects-additional.md ("Creating a Validator object", "Modifying global objects in the Web Designer"), docs/mongoose/guides/ido-development.md ("Adding or editing validators", the In Collection page link), the EXP-085 record and outcome (the Global Objects dialog, Tab commits, Cancel readbacks, the Save toast), the EXP-069-R4 outcome and the EXP-078 record (the FX_HelloWorld01 columns FX_Code, FX_Label, FX_Address) before browser interaction.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-087-hello-world-part-5-section-8-fx-customerid-in-collection-validator.md and evidence/EXP-087/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If it expires, follow the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure once and end the task; never sign in inside the portal's embedded app frame (refused, EXP-080-R2) but use the procedure's top-level portal navigation. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt or dialog open across tasks unless the coordinator's next task explicitly continues it.

Preflight and gates: the Designer is in User scope and clean with FX_Orders open (open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry if needed). Open Designer Edit > Validator once read-only, record the dialog layout (list, list controls, Properties pane, buttons) and whether FX_CustomerID exists, and close it with its Cancel control. If FX_CustomerID already exists, record it and stop blocked without creating anything.

Creation: open Edit > Validator once, use the list New (+) control once, enter the Name FX_CustomerID, confirm the name prompt with its OK once, and record the new property sheet. Set Type In Collection (choose from its list, Tab once, verify). Open the Parameters ellipsis once and record the parameters dialog layout before changing anything.

Parameters: set IDO FX_HelloWorld01 (choose from its list, or type the exact name if the list is empty, then Tab and verify). Open the Set Prop properties ellipsis once; use New once per output and set Target %1 with Value FX_Label, then Target %2 with Value FX_Address (choose each Value from its list; type each Target exactly; Tab and verify each), confirming each output with its OK once. Under In Collection Only open the Property ellipsis once and choose FX_Code, OK once. In the Error Message field enter mIsNotAValid (choose it from a list if one is offered, otherwise type it), Tab and verify. Record the resulting parameter string verbatim if the dialog shows one. Then confirm the nested dialogs with OK once each back to the Global Objects dialog, and that dialog with OK once; record each response and whether the Designer Save became enabled.
Message stop rule: if any prompt offers to create a string or message (for example for mIsNotAValid), answer No once, leave the Error Message blank, record it, and continue; never create a string.

Readback: open Edit > Validator once, select FX_CustomerID, record every visible property (Type and the Parameters value verbatim; open the Parameters ellipsis once read-only only if the value is not fully visible, and close it with Cancel), and close the dialog with Cancel.

Correction contingency, at most once and only for a value that reads blank or wrong: in that dialog select FX_CustomerID, correct only that value (commit with Tab, verify), confirm with OK, and repeat the readback once.
Perform exactly one Designer Save through the native toolbar Save and record the native response verbatim; if Save is disabled at that point, record it and make no Save.

Close the clean FX_Orders Designer Form once through its Form-tab control and reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry; read FX_CustomerID back once more through Edit > Validator (closing with Cancel); confirm no FX_Orders component changed (the Designer stays clean).

Capture screenshots of the gate list, the new property sheet, the parameters dialog before and after filling, each Set Prop output before OK, the In Collection Only Property, the Error Message, each readback, the Save and the reopened readback.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.

Never claim runtime validation behavior, database durability or replay verification from Designer readbacks.

FX_CustomerID created once through New with Type In Collection; Parameters IDO FX_HelloWorld01, outputs %1 = FX_Label and %2 = FX_Address, In Collection Only Property FX_Code, Error Message mIsNotAValid (or blank with the No answer recorded), each committed with Tab before OK; each dialog confirmed once. Evidence: dialog screenshots before each OK.

The readback shows Type In Collection and the Parameters value verbatim containing FX_HelloWorld01, FX_Code, %1, FX_Label, %2 and FX_Address (corrections, if any, within the contingency); exactly one Designer Save with its native response, or Save disabled recorded. Evidence: readback and Save screenshots.
The clean Form closed once and reopened once; the reopened readback matches AC-3; no component changed; no other validator changed. Evidence: reopen readback screenshots.

The final EXP-087 report gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-4, the complete action audit with exact counts (validators created 1, New 1, Set Prop outputs 2, dialog OKs, Tab commits, string prompts and answers, contingency corrections, Designer Save at most 1, Designer close/reopen 1, zero component changes, zero runtime actions, zero checkout actions, re-login count), the worker-written-file inventory and the final state. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are observed only.
